prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B019 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The first round did not weaken the scientific case, and no member challenged its merit or maturity. The chain from proglucagon processing and human incretin physiology, through identification of the active truncated peptide and receptor biology, to long-acting agonists and large randomized outcome trials is independently confirmed and still widening, so recognition is timely. A single achievement with three names stays inside the cap and gives a clean citation. Adding a second part would force someone out of a trio that is already tight, and no second candidate has a cleaner credit position than B019 combined with a manageable attribution risk.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weak point and the first round did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36/37) form against Habener's group is contested, and none of us can settle it from the supplied record. Knudsen's acylated-analogue design is what made the drugs practical, and the cap leaves her out. A discovery-side prize can therefore be criticised for omitting the step that delivered the benefit. I treat both as real costs that I accept deliberately. If the committee concluded that the record does not support Mojsov, I would not reach for a fourth name but would move to Drucker and Holst with Knudsen as the third, or to a Holst and Drucker pair.

responses.point: Linnarsson keeps Mojsov over Knudsen because the citation should rest on discovery of the active peptide, would put the drug-development step in the framing of the citation, and accepts that Knudsen is the natural replacement if the record weakens Mojsov's claim.
responses.response: I agree with the structure of this answer and, after round 1, I hold the same position. The reasoning is discovery first, drug design acknowledged in the wording, and a pre-agreed substitution rule if the priority record fails. That answers the chair's first two questions without ruling on the Habener dispute. The new point I would add is that the substitution rule should be decided now. If we leave it to the vote, the third place could split the support for an otherwise unanimous configuration. I would therefore fix it as Knudsen replacing Mojsov, not as a vote between a pair and a trio.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius argues that Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide design is arguably as decisive for patients as the physiology, but in round 1 she still signed the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio, and she says that B040 is the second achievement she would support while B019 should stand alone if the union has to stay at three.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen argument seriously and I do not dismiss it as industrial. Without half-life engineering the physiology would not have reached patients at scale. My difficulty is that the prize cannot honour both discoveries within three people without removing Holst or Drucker, whose physiology and biology are the secure core. So my answer to her is to keep the physiologists and let the citation say that the discoveries made incretin therapies possible. On her second point we agree. If the union has to stay at three, B019 stands alone. A B040 part would reduce B019 to one or two names, and I do not think the scientific gain justifies that.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, disagrees with my TOR position because he sees the Schreiber FKBP12-rapamycin step as only part of the target identification, and he treats B030 as his first alternative and B012 as the second, while saying that B012 should follow B019 and not share the prize.
responses.response: On TOR I stand by what I said in round 1. Every pair in B027 leaves out someone with a real claim, so I rank it below candidates with clearer allocations. On the chair's question about a second part, I agree with him that B012 should follow B019 and not share it. The allocation problem is at the core of that candidate, not at the margin, and the committee would be choosing among Nagel, Hegemann, Deisseroth, Boyden and Bamberg without a record that decides it. I also hold to my view that B030 is not yet ready as a pair. The prize would be either for CAR engineering or for cell therapy more broadly, and that choice has not been made.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics second with Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, and names Holst and Drucker as a fallback pair for B019, saying that the third place is a real choice between Mojsov and Knudsen.
responses.response: I agree that the choice of the third place is real and that Holst and Drucker are the most secure pair. I part from him on whether B012 can take a prize slot this year. His trio is the most defensible one, but Boyden's neuronal demonstration and Bamberg's earlier channelrhodopsin work are core priority claims, not marginal ones, and any trio would leave the decision contested. The clinical case is also limited to early retinal work. I also see his fallback pair as a coherent prize if the record fails on Mojsov, but I would choose Knudsen as a third name before accepting a two-person prize.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks the unfolded protein response (B040) second, argues that Walter and Mori are a clean pair and that mechanism-led impact is a weakness only on a narrow reading of the prize, and he would put Hall alone as the clearest TOR attribution.
responses.response: I agree that B040 has the cleanest credit of any candidate outside B019, and I keep it as my first alternative for that reason. I disagree that the lack of a therapy is only a narrow reading. For a Medicine prize I want a disease link that is more than implied, and for B040 the integrated stress response and the PERK and ATF6 work of Ron and Kaufman complicate a two-person claim that looks clean. That is why I would keep it as the best basic-science alternative and not as a part to pair with B019. On TOR, a Hall-alone prize is clearer than a pair but would exclude the discoverers of the rapamycin target step, so I still would not lead with it.

uncertainties: Whether the record supports Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against Habener's group. I could not verify this from the supplied files and my position depends on it.

Whether the committee will accept a citation that credits discovery of the active peptide and incretin physiology while only acknowledging the long-acting analogue step, or will judge that to under-credit the drug development.

Whether B040 should outrank therapy-linked candidates such as B030 as the second choice if the committee later wants a second achievement, which depends on how it weighs conceptual cleanliness against clinical impact.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure. My profile records co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen and a postdoctoral period in Christopher Burge's group, and none of them is a credited name in my configuration or on the shortlist. My RNA processing and splicing work is topically near B028, which is not in my preferred configuration, and topic proximity alone is not a conflict. I do not request recusal.
